A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same algebraic framework and diagonal-SSM case study. All 28 pages of each version, including Appendices A–J, are readable and support comparison of the text, equations, figures, and tables.

before.justification: v1 reports theoretical results and mathematical constructions, including Appendices H and J, but no original experimental, simulation, user-study, or data-analysis outcomes.

after.justification: v3 remains a theoretical paper. Its appendix case studies contain proofs and explicit constructions, without original empirical outcomes.

M1.justification: The cores, cascade wiring, acceptance machinery, and recurrence constructions are retained. Renaming the underlying cascade an algebraic semi-RNN and revising symbols and wiring indices do not introduce a different computational procedure.

E1.justification: Neither version trains or evaluates on datasets. The same architecture families, arithmetic regimes, and theoretical parity and modular-counting examples remain.

E2.justification: Neither version reports evaluated baseline comparisons. The comparisons with prior expressivity theorems are retained; the additional introductory citation does not introduce an evaluated comparator.

E3.justification: No empirical evaluation protocol is introduced or revised. The arithmetic assumptions, recurrence-consistent evaluation requirements, and four-bit parity construction in Example J.18 remain unchanged.

E4.justification: The clamped-recurrence analysis in Appendix H and diagonal-SSM case study in Appendix J address the same questions. No ablations, robustness tests, sensitivity analyses, or additional case studies are introduced.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated experiments, seeds, confidence intervals, significance tests, or statistical uncertainty estimates.

E6.justification: Table 2 revises theoretical result entries: the containment classes for signed floating point and unsigned integers change from ordinary pseudovariety joins to explicitly wreath-closed pseudovarieties. The subgroup entries, counting conclusions, and explicit parity construction remain unchanged. These are theoretical classifications, not performance measurements.

T1.justification: Table 2 and Remark J.15 introduce explicit wreath-closure definitions in place of the earlier join formulation. v3 also adds an odd-prime-divisor proof sketch for the existing Corollary J.17 and corrects wiring indices. The main factorization and cascade theorems remain substantively unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same contributions: an algebraic characterization of recurrent models, the importance of arithmetic semantics, and the contrasting counting capabilities illustrated by diagonal SSMs.

C2.justification: The discussion beneath Table 2 replaces v1's assertion of the same pseudovariety at the single-core level with a clearer distinction between single-core group content and the shared wreath-closed language class. Appendix C's limitations concerning learnability, finite precision, and attention architectures are retained.

D1.justification: The architecture specifications, arithmetic semantics, and explicit construction parameters in the appendices are retained. No implementation resources, hardware details, training information, or code/data access instructions are added.

R1.justification: The introduction additionally credits the already-cited Karuvally et al. (2025) among developments in more expressive linear RNNs. The revised Table 2 discussion connects its closure terminology to Eilenberg's closed M-varieties. The bibliography otherwise contains the same works.

P1.justification: v3 systematically changes Q/q to Z/z and distinguishes algebraic semi-RNNs from complete RNN automata. It adds short explanatory remarks and makes local wording edits while retaining the document's organization. The symbol replacement introduces a GRU gate/state naming collision in Appendix D.

P2.justification: Figure 1 updates wiring labels, and Figure 2 adopts the revised state notation. The same figures and tables remain, with modest spacing and page-flow changes, including Appendix E beginning on page 16 instead of page 17.

improvement.justification: The explicit wreath-closure formulation around Table 2 and the added proof of Corollary J.17 improve the precision and inspectability of the existing argument. The semi-RNN terminology also clarifies the formal objects. These limited gains outweigh the new GRU notation ambiguity in Appendix D, although the inconsistency between Theorem J.13 and Remark J.15 concerning group divisors remains unresolved.
